definition: Emerging standards for communication between independent agents across vendors and organizations: capability discovery, task delegation, and status exchange.
details: Emerging standards for communication between independent agents across vendors and organizations: capability discovery, task delegation, and status exchange. Complementary to MCP: MCP connects agents to tools; A2A connects agents to each other.

explainer.lead: A2A, or Agent-to-Agent Protocols, are emerging standards that let independent AI agents work together across vendors and organizations. They provide a common way to discover what another agent can do, hand it a task, and follow its progress.

tiers.eli5: Imagine asking a friend to help with a project. First you find out what they are good at, then you give them a job, and then they tell you how it is going. A2A gives AI helpers a shared way to do those same things, even when different people or companies made them.
tiers.practitioner: In a multi-agent deployment, A2A handles capability discovery, task delegation, and status exchange between independent agents. Keep its boundary with MCP clear: MCP connects an agent to tools, while A2A connects agents to one another. Because these standards are emerging, do not assume that different vendors will expose identical capabilities or behavior.
tiers.paperLevel: A2A can be summarized as cross-vendor, cross-organization agent interaction = capability discovery + task delegation + status exchange. It concerns communication between independent agents, whereas MCP concerns agent-to-tool communication. The standards are emerging, and the term alone does not specify a message schema, transport mechanism, or interoperability guarantee.

explainer.example: A company's planning agent needs a specialist agent operated by another organization. It discovers that the specialist can analyze a particular kind of request, delegates that request, and then receives status updates instead of having to poll an opaque, vendor-specific interface.
explainer.intuition: Independent agents need more than a way to call tools: they need a shared etiquette for working with one another. A2A supplies that etiquette so one agent can find a suitable peer, delegate work, and track what happens.
howItWorks: One agent discovers the capabilities offered by another agent.
It selects an agent that can handle the required work.
It delegates a task to that agent.
The agents exchange status information as the work proceeds.
The interaction can cross vendor and organizational boundaries.
explainer.whyItMatters: A2A aims to make agents built by different vendors and organizations interoperable. That can reduce custom one-off integrations when tasks need to move between independent agents.
misconceptions: A2A is not the same as MCP: MCP connects agents to tools, while A2A connects agents to other agents.
A2A is not a single agent or an agent architecture; it refers to emerging communication standards.
Capability discovery does not itself perform a task; delegation and status exchange are separate parts of the interaction.
